passage: The rumour was that I cheated in the unit test. I'm Varun, and I hadn't. Someone started it in a group chat, and by the next morning people were whispering as I walked in. My first instinct was to shout at the whole class. My second was to stay home forever. My chest was tight, and I couldn't eat breakfast. But I sat on the stairs and told myself to breathe. I didn't start a rumour back, though I could think of a few. I told my mother that evening and she came to school with me. I showed my teacher my rough work and the marks list, and posted once in the class chat, "I didn't cheat. My rough work is with the teacher." Nitin sat next to me at lunch the whole week. That helped more than any argument.

qa.q: What was the rumour about Varun?
qa.a: The rumour was that Varun cheated in the unit test.

qa.q: What were Varun's two first instincts, and what was the feeling underneath?
qa.a: Varun wanted to shout at the whole class or stay home forever, and felt afraid: a tight chest and no appetite for breakfast.

qa.q: What did Varun do that helped?
qa.a: Varun calmed down, told their mother, showed the teacher the rough work and the marks list, corrected it once in the chat and did not spread a rumour back.

qa.q: How might Nitin have seen the rumour about Varun?
qa.a: Probably as not worth believing, since Nitin sat next to Varun at lunch the whole week; that steady company said more than any argument.

grounding: A false rumour spreads about Varun; Varun stays calm, tells their mother and the teacher, corrects it once with facts and leans on a real friend.

passage:
Tuesday. The rumour was already everywhere by second period: Vaibhav had stolen money from the science lab box. It wasn't true. He'd only been in the lab to return a beaker. Some boys stopped talking when he walked past. His hands went cold. He wanted to shout at all of them, or never come back.
Wednesday. He told Papa at breakfast, voice shaking. Papa put his tea down. "We'll go together." At school, the class teacher, Ms Joshi, listened and checked the lab register. Vaibhav had signed out at 11:02, before the box was even opened.
Thursday. Ms Joshi said it clearly in class: "The rumour about Vaibhav is false. Please stop." Vaibhav added one line in the class group: "I didn't take anything. The lab register shows I left before the box was opened." Then he muted the group.
His friend Gautam sat next to him all day, like nothing had changed. That helped more than anything.

qa.q: What time did Vaibhav sign out of the lab?
How did Vaibhav feel when he heard the rumour?
qa.a: He felt frightened and angry, his hands going cold, torn between shouting at everyone and disappearing.

qa.q: Which steps helped stop the rumour?
qa.a: Telling Papa, going to Ms Joshi, checking the register, correcting it once with facts, and staying near Gautam.

qa.q: How does Gautam show he sees the rumour?
qa.a: Gautam treats it as false and sits with Vaibhav all day as usual, showing loyalty.

grounding: A teen facing a false rumour stays calm, tells a parent and teacher, corrects it once with facts, and leans on a real friend.

passage:
Chinmay, you look like you want to break your phone. Sit with me.
When I was fifteen, in our Nashik school, a girl in my class spread a story that I'd been thrown out of my old school for cheating. Not one word of it was true. Within two days, girls stopped sitting near me. I heard whispers on the stairs.
I wanted to scream. I also wanted to spread something worse about her. I knew things.
That night I told my mother. She didn't shout. The next day she came with me to the headmistress, and together we showed my old school's leaving certificate with the conduct remark: "Excellent." That was the turning point.
The headmistress spoke to the class. I said only one thing: "I was never thrown out. Here is my certificate." I didn't say a word about the other girl.
My two real friends stayed close. The rumour died in a week. Your Sangeeta Aaji learned: facts, calm, and good friends.

qa.q: What did the rumour claim about young Sangeeta?
qa.a: That she had been thrown out of her old school for cheating.

qa.q: How did young Sangeeta feel when the whispers started?
qa.a: She felt frightened and furious, wanting to scream and even to spread something worse about the other girl.

qa.q: What was the turning point, and why did it work?
qa.a: Going to the headmistress with her mother and the leaving certificate let her correct the rumour once with facts, without starting a counter-rumour.

qa.q: How might the girl who spread the rumour have felt when the headmistress spoke?
qa.a: She probably felt exposed and uncomfortable, especially since Sangeeta didn't attack her back.

grounding: An elder recalls a false rumour at school and staying calm, telling a parent and teacher, correcting it once with facts and leaning on friends.
